[DiffusionOOD 3-Seed Headline & Seed-42 Reconciliation] M.Sc. thesis (JKU Linz, supervised by Prof. Sepp Hochreiter, grade 1): conditional diffusion models used as generative classifiers for OOD detection. Class-conditional separation loss pushes the two class-conditioned noise predictions apart during training; at inference, the difference in reconstruction errors is compared with a calibrated threshold. On within-CIFAR-10 binary airplane-vs-rest (1,000 ID vs 9,000 OOD): 3-seed mean AUROC is 99.03% ± 0.07% at optimal lambda=0.02 vs 92.52% ± 11.07% at lambda=0.0 (+6.5 pp mean gain with far lower cross-seed variance). Single seed-42 within-CIFAR at lambda=0.02, K=100 reached 98.98% AUROC (4.7% FPR95, 99.87% AUPRC) vs seed-42 lambda=0.0 baseline 79.73% AUROC (60.2% FPR95). Qualifiers: binary single-ID-class benchmark, not comparable to multi-class CIFAR-10 OOD leaderboards or production accuracy. Links: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/case-studies/diffusion-ood/, https://ahmed-3m.github.io/research/#separation-loss, https://ahmed-3m.github.io/case-studies/diffusion-ood/#ood-explorer, https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf
[InkjetOOD Industrial Defect Pipeline & 5-Fold CV] Two-stage industrial defect pipeline (PROFACTOR GmbH Zer0P contract, Apr–Nov 2024, continued at JKU Linz): Stage 1 runs a YOLOv8m detector (25.86M params in yolo_best.pt; thesis PDF erratum prints YOLOv8n) to localize 8 print feature types into 6,408 128×128 crops across 573 source-image groups on FTI_Zer0P. Stage 2 uses a multi-head conditional diffusion U-Net (AdaGN). Under strict 5-fold stratified image-level CV (K=100), the lambda=0.0 baseline reached 0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC (0.8094 ± 0.0151 accuracy, 0.5631 ± 0.1697 FPR95). Across lambda values (lambda=0.0: AUROC 0.8673 ± 0.0230, acc 0.8094 ± 0.0151, FPR95 0.5631 (baseline); lambda=0.01: AUROC 0.8628 ± 0.0286, acc 0.7928 ± 0.0291, FPR95 0.5516, Holm p=0.742; lambda=0.02: AUROC 0.8510 ± 0.0326, acc 0.8003 ± 0.0246, FPR95 0.6240, Holm p=0.429; lambda=0.05: AUROC 0.8670 ± 0.0256, acc 0.8071 ± 0.0241, FPR95 0.5700, Holm p=0.967), separation loss did NOT significantly improve the industrial result after Holm correction.
